chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Kazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Jabir ibn Abdullah: 'O Jabir! This is the month of Ramadan. Whoever fasts its day, stands in prayer from its night, keeps his belly and private parts chaste, and restrains his tongue, will emerge from his sins as he emerged from the month.' So Jabir said: 'O Messenger of Allah! How beautiful is this hadith!' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Jabir! And how severe/difficult are these conditions.'

key_terms.عَفَّ بَطْنُهُ وَ فَرْجُهُ: Kept his belly and private parts chaste

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for complete forgiveness of sins during Ramadan according to the Prophet (SAWW)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes that Ramadan fasting is not merely abstention from food but a holistic discipline involving the guarding of the stomach, private parts, and tongue, leading to a complete cleansing of sins. The Prophet’s follow-up remark underscores the rigorous nature of these conditions, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that true spiritual purification requires active, conscious effort across all faculties. This narrative serves as a practical guide for believers to elevate their worship beyond ritualistic form to comprehensive moral and spiritual excellence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Jabir Bin Abdullah; ‘O Jabir! This is the Month of Ramazan. The one who Fasts during its days, and stands in response (for Prayers) during its nights, and excuses his belly and his private parts, and restrains his tongue, would come out from his sins just as he comes out from the month’. So Jabir said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! How beautiful is this Hadeeth!’ So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Jabir! And how difficult are these stipulations (conditions)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once said to Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, “O Jabir, this is the month of Ramadan. Anyone who fasts during its days, stands for salat (prayer) during its nights, maintains his stomach and private parts chastely and controls his tongue, comes out of his sins just like his coming out of the month.” Jabir then said, “How beautiful is this Hadith, O the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.” The Messenger of Allah said, “O Jabir, how strict these conditions are!”’”
